name: Datadog
scope_notes: IP documentation differs on entitlement (Pro+ via support vs Enterprise). Confirm contract. AWS WIF requires supported integration/configuration.

controls.name: Application key scopes
controls.what: Restricts an application key to the listed authorization scopes instead of all of its owner's permissions.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Application Keys (edit key scopes); Key Management API
controls.quote: Scoped application keys are granted only the scopes specified by the user

controls.name: API Keys Write permission
controls.what: Only roles holding api_keys_write can create or rename API keys (Admin role by default).
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Roles (custom roles)
controls.plan: Custom roles may require an eligible plan (not confirmed)
controls.quote: Create and rename API Keys for your organization.

controls.name: User App Keys / Org App Keys Write permissions
controls.what: Controls who can create and manage their own application keys (user_app_keys) or anyone's keys (org_app_keys_write).
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Roles
controls.quote: View and manage Application Keys owned by the user.

controls.name: Service Account Write permission
controls.what: Limits who can create, disable and use service accounts that own application keys.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Roles; Organization Settings > Service Accounts
controls.quote: Create, disable, and use Service Accounts in your organization.

controls.name: One-Time Read (OTR) mode
controls.what: Shows application key secrets only once at creation; becomes permanent after 3 months enabled.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Application Keys (requires org_app_keys_write + org_management)
controls.quote: When OTR mode is enabled, application key secrets are only displayed once during creation.

controls.name: Actions API access (per application key)
controls.what: Application keys cannot call the Actions APIs unless explicitly enabled per key.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Application Keys or API
controls.quote: By default, application keys cannot be used with these APIs.

controls.name: IP Allowlist
controls.what: Blocks UI, public API and OAuth app access from IPs outside the list; Agent intake and some endpoints are exempt.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Security > IP Allowlist; IP Allowlist API; Terraform ip_allowlist (Org Management permission)
controls.plan: Pro+ or Enterprise, enabled via support (API reference says Enterprise)
controls.quote: When the IP allowlist is enabled, only IP addresses or CIDR ranges in the allowlist can access the Datadog API and UI.

controls.name: Revoke API key / application key
controls.what: Revoked API keys can be restored for 7 days; application key revocation is permanent.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > API Keys / Application Keys; Key Management API
controls.quote: Revoking an application key is permanent.

controls.name: Disable OAuth access for an application
controls.what: Turns off an OAuth app and revokes it for all users in the org.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > OAuth Apps (Admin role or org_authorized_apps_read/write)
controls.quote: Disabling OAuth access for an application revokes access to this application for all users in your organization.

controls.name: Revoke a user's OAuth access
controls.what: Removes one user's authorization for an OAuth app; the user can re-authorize.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > OAuth Apps
controls.quote: Revoking a user's OAuth access to an application removes all access to that application.

controls.name: Workload Identity Federation identity and intake mappings
controls.what: Only AWS role ARNs matched by a mapping can authenticate, and each identity mapping grants exactly one Datadog user or service account's permissions.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Workload Identity Federation > Identity Mappings / Intake Mappings; cloud_auth API
controls.plan: Not stated on page; requires Datadog-AWS integration
controls.quote: Each mapping grants a cloud role the permissions of a specific Datadog user or service account.

controls.name: Workload Identity Federation Write permission
controls.what: Only roles with this permission can add, change or remove federation mappings (Admin role by default).
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Roles
controls.quote: Add, update, and remove workload identity federation configurations

controls.name: Client Tokens Write permission
controls.what: Only roles with client_tokens_write can create or edit client tokens (Standard role by default).
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Roles; Organization Settings > Client Tokens

controls.name: Revoke a token (PAT)
controls.what: Owner or admin revokes a PAT; it stops authenticating within seconds.
controls.setting: Personal Settings > Access Tokens or Organization Settings > Access Tokens > Revoke Token; DELETE /api/v2/personal_access_tokens/<PAT_ID>

controls.name: Revoke a token (SAT)
controls.what: Admin revokes a SAT; it stops authenticating within seconds.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Service Accounts > (account) > Revoke, or Organization Settings > Access Tokens; DELETE /api/v2/service_accounts/<SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID>/access_tokens/<TOKEN_ID>

controls.name: Disable existing members
controls.what: Disabling a user revokes all of their PATs immediately.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Users > Disable

controls.name: User App Keys (user_app_keys) permission
controls.what: Only roles with user_app_keys can create PATs; remove it from a role to stop its members creating PATs.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Roles (permission user_app_keys)

controls.name: Service Account Write (service_account_write) permission
controls.what: Only roles with service_account_write (or org_app_keys_write) can create SATs.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Roles (permission service_account_write)

controls.name: Token scopes
controls.what: Each PAT or SAT must have at least one scope and can only do what its scopes allow.
controls.setting: Select Scopes when creating or editing a token

controls.name: Mandatory PAT time-to-live
controls.what: Every PAT expires between 24 hours and one year after creation; expired tokens are revoked automatically.
controls.setting: Expiration Date at creation (fixed by Datadog bounds)

controls.name: Restrictions on token-authenticated API calls
controls.what: A PAT or SAT cannot create application keys, and can only mint tokens with a subset of its scopes and no longer TTL.
controls.setting: Built in

controls.name: IP Allowlist
controls.what: Org-wide allowlist blocks API calls from IPs outside the list, including token-authenticated calls.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Security > IP Allowlist; IP Allowlist API

controls.name: Unused Application Keys (Governance Console control)
controls.what: Detects application keys unused for a set period (default 30 days) and can automatically revoke them.
controls.setting: Governance Console > Controls > Unused Application Keys > Enforce control

controls.name: Unused API Keys (Governance Console control)
controls.what: Detects API keys unused for a set period and can automatically revoke them.
controls.setting: Governance Console > Controls > Unused API Keys > Enforce control

controls.name: Leaked API Keys (Governance Console control)
controls.what: Detects active API keys found exposed publicly by Datadog token leak detection, with optional enforcement.
controls.setting: Governance Console > Controls > Leaked API Keys

no_control.what: No expiration or maximum lifetime for API or application keys.
No expiration for RUM client tokens, and they survive deactivation of the creating user.
no_control.quote: When a user who created a client token is deactivated, the client token remains active.

no_control.what: IP restriction for a single token; the IP allowlist is org-wide only.
IP restriction for a single token; the IP allowlist is org-wide only.

controls_unknown: No org setting found that blocks personal application keys or forces service-account-only keys.

Whether the IP allowlist applies to API-key and client-token requests outside telemetry intake is not stated; entitlement differs between account docs (Pro+/Enterprise) and API reference (Enterprise).
Plan requirement for Agent-based WIF: current WIF page lists no tier; earlier material says Enterprise-only and preview.
How to delete or disable an identity mapping is not documented on the WIF page; intake mappings are deleted via API.
Whether custom roles (needed to narrow these permissions) require a specific plan was not confirmed.
